correctness.rationale: Exact 2D Gaussian integration of conditional two-camera union probability yields a difference of two exponentials. Its derivative has at most one positive zero in separation and gives the exact co-location threshold. Differentiating squared optimal separation in k=w²/r² yields equation L=T; the sign is controlled by a quartic whose coefficients have one sign change and hence one positive root. This proves a unique detection-width peak. The p→0 limit uses k0∼2/p and kpeak∼2e/p. Standalone checker passed 11,156 checks including 598 rational identities and nine independent spatial quadratures; finite tests support, not prove, universal claims.

The 2008 Litvak report gives a sufficient no-overlap criterion with constant sensitivity within one-dimensional intervals, not a smooth-detection two-dimensional complete classification.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general spatial integral logically allows this model to be substituted but does not itself assert the later sharp optimization conclusions. In particular, strict uniqueness of the best detector width follows from a separate one-positive-root factorization. No stronger theorem found that would make these assertions an already stated special case. A broad facility-location theorem outside inspected literature is a residual priority risk.

value.rationale: Camera traps sample heterogeneous habitat, and both sensor overlap and missed detections affect the number of distinct individuals observed. The exact co-location boundary and nonmonotonic optimal physical separation reveal three operationally different sensitivity regimes; the unique intermediate optimum and rare-detection scaling are not just evaluating a trivial constant or changing notation. They provide a compact benchmark for deciding whether two symmetric cameras should overlap when detection width or sensitivity changes. The result is restricted and does not claim field calibration or estimator optimality.
